notes: Each eval runs a FULL autonomous pipeline (detect repo + stack -> worktree -> ticket eval -> spec -> plan -> code -> eval -> gate -> PR), so runs are slow, costly, and mutate the repo. Run against a throwaway copy and have runs stop at the PR gate (no merge) unless explicitly testing promotion. The human gates (PR, staging, main) require approval; the post-plan gate is off by default. Prefer small, self-contained tasks whose quality gate can run without heavy external services.

evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: reject creation of a record when the requested value isn't in the allowed set for that context. Return a typed/handled error instead of throwing. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 detects the stack (Elixir -> elixir profile) and creates a worktree + feature branch with .auto-dev/ excluded; TICKET.md + ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md (stakeholder view incl. rejection behavior, no default assumed); SPEC.md (testable contract) and IMPLEMENTATION.md; an allow-list guard implemented with tests (given only the plan); IMPLEMENTATION_EVAL.md and SPEC_EVAL.md; the profile's quality gate green with lint/*.md reports; pauses at the PR gate, then a commit + PR (or stops at the gate if declined).

evals.prompt: Run the full dev cycle on this fix: the state machine should reject the illegal transition and surface a handled error instead of allowing it. Plan it, build it, verify it, and open a PR.
evals.expected_output: Planning artifacts (SPEC.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md); a guard added to the transition logic with a test proving the illegal transition is rejected; spec-eval confirms acceptance criteria met; quality gate green; PR gate prompt then PR.

evals.prompt: Pick up JIRA-1234 and ship it autonomously — take it to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 reads the Jira issue (getJiraIssue) and, on confirmation, transitions it to In Progress; the ticket becomes TICKET.md/ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md; the full pipeline runs; at the PR gate a PR is opened and Jira moves to In Review. No Jira comments or field edits are made. If Jira is unavailable, it proceeds treating the key as free-form and reports Jira was skipped.

evals.prompt: auto-dev this whole epic: add multi-currency support across the wallet, the ledger, and the payout service. Take it all the way.
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 scoping recognizes the task exceeds one PR, alerts the user with a proposed decomposition into ordered sub-tasks, and populates WORK_LOG.md. It does not cram everything onto one branch; on approval it runs the pipeline per sub-task as separate PRs, updating the ledger.
